# MCP registry

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P4 · Agents everywhere](../README.md#phase-4--agents-everywhere) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:mcp-registry` · **Epic:** [#176](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/176) · **Tickets:** 10 (2S 8M)

The CP keeps a versioned registry of approved MCP servers: transport, endpoint or launch command, owner team, approved tools, canonical tool pins and per-platform binary integrity. Widening changes, rollbacks included, go through the Phase 2 approvals flow. Pinned workers receive the registry as a signed-bundle section, so the gateway and `warden mcp` enforce one central list per tool, on tools/call. The registry only narrows MCP traffic: it never adds egress allowlist entries, and it is off until an operator turns it on.

## How we build it

- Gate and back-compat: new CP-local `console.mcpRegistry: {enabled: false, maxServers: 500, maxToolsPerVersion: 1000}` in the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig (`json:"-"`, read only from the operator --config). When enabled, startup fails with an error naming the missing item unless `--state-dir`, console.auth=oidc, `console.adminAudit.enabled=true`, `--policy-store=versioned` and `--bundles=offer|require` are all set. When disabled, no migration runs, /dashboard/api/mcp/* returns 404, no section is published, and /policy plus the legacy wire stay byte-identical. Without a registry, worker `mcp.servers` and the wedge's `--verify-*` flags behave exactly as today.
- Data model (new package internal/mcpregistry holds types, Validate, Diff, Classify, the section wire and `Compiled`, with no DB imports; the SQLite store lives in new internal/mcpregistry/sqlitestore on cpstate migration `mcp_registry/0001`): `mcp_servers(id slug [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62} immutable, name, owner_team, state active|disabled, current_version, created_at)` holds identity only. Append-only `mcp_server_versions(server_id, version, transport http|sse|ws|stdio, url, command, args_json, env_json {ENV_NAME: placeholder}, per_user_provider, approved_tools_json, tool_pins_json {tool: c1:<hex>}, integrity_json {"<GOOS>/<GOARCH>"|"any": {sha256, ed25519PublicKey, ed25519Signature}}, label, draft_id, created_by_sub, created_at, doc_sha256)`, UNIQUE(server_id, version). Every endpoint- or launch-relevant field is on the version, so diff, approvals and rollback all work on whole versions. One row `mcp_registry_meta(revision, mode off|monitor|enforce, unregistered_server deny|allow, require_stdio_integrity, require_pin_verified)`. Approvers come from change_approvals through draft_id, not an approved_by column. Every apply, rollback, disable, enable or settings change bumps `revision` in the same transaction. A conformance suite `mcpregistrytest.Run(t, newStore)` lets p5-postgres-ha add its own store.
- Validation: http/sse/ws urls are absolute https (http only for loopback), with no userinfo and no query value matching the internal/scan credential detectors. Only one active http/sse/ws server may use a given host, because the forward-proxy session key is `agentID:domain` and cannot tell paths apart. stdio needs an absolute `command`. args and labels are scanned with the same detectors and rejected on a match. env keys match ^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$ and are not on a reserved list (PATH, LD_*, DYLD_*, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR); env values must equal a `secrets[].placeholder` in the live settings, so a real credential is never stored or handed to a child process. `per_user_provider` must be a configured `consent.providers[].id` (W-P3-BRKR-01). Integrity hex is checked by new shared `config.ValidateMCPIntegrity` (sha256 64 hex, public key 64 hex and not all-zero, signature 128 hex and needs a key), which `validateMCPServers` also adopts. With require_stdio_integrity (default true), a stdio version needs at least one integrity entry. Caps: 500 servers, 1000 approved tools per version, 64 args of at most 1024 bytes, 32 env entries, and a projected section of at most 1 MiB. Error messages name the field and index, never the value.
- Pins: new `mcp.ToolPin(name, description string, inputSchema json.RawMessage) (string, error)` = `c1:` + sha256 hex over canonical JSON (decode with UseNumber, re-encode with sorted keys and no whitespace) of {name, description, inputSchema}. Pinning the description catches tool poisoning after approval, and canonical form stops false drift when a server re-serialises its schema. The `c1:` prefix lets a later algorithm be added without migrating stored pins. `gateway.hashSchema` stays unchanged for existing inventory and baselines. ToolInfo, InventoryItem and therefore analytics.MCPSnapshot gain `Pin`, and the gateway inventory is keyed by (server, tool), so import uses the same algorithm and tools with the same name on two servers no longer overwrite each other.
- REST under `/dashboard/api/mcp/*` (admin routes stay under /dashboard/api/*; API keys reach them through the W-P2-APIK-02 Scope column), every route with an authz row (Action `mcp_registry.<verb>`, Target `mcp_registry`, Audited on writes, explicit Scope): `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/servers`, `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}`, `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}/versions`, `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}/versions/{v}`, `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}/versions/{v}/diff?against={w}` (default v-1), `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/observed?host=`, `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/registry/settings` (mcp:read, viewer); `POST /dashboard/api/mcp/servers`, `POST /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}/versions`, `POST /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}/rollback {version}`, `POST /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}/disable`, `POST /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}/enable`, `PUT /dashboard/api/mcp/registry/settings` (mcp:write, editor minimum). There is no hard delete; disable is the delete. Admin is required to create or enable a server, to change transport, url, command, args, env, integrity or per_user_provider, and to lower any registry setting. Server writes need `If-Match: "v<current_version>"` and settings writes `If-Match: "r<revision>"`: 409 `registry_conflict` when stale, 428 when missing. Responses: 201/200 {server, version, revision} when applied, 202 {draft_id, revision, state, widening, reasons} with Location when held, 422 {error, field} on validation failure. Example: POST /dashboard/api/mcp/servers {id:"linear", transport:"http", url:"https://mcp.linear.app/mcp", approvedTools:["list_issues"], toolPins:{"list_issues":"c1:ab12.."}} returns 202 when approvals are on and 201 when they are off.
- Approvals: register target `mcp_registry` (target_ref = server id, or `settings`) with a Classifier and an Applier using the W-P2-APPR-08 target registry. `mcpregistry.Classify(current, candidate)` is pure and compares against the live current version, rollbacks included. Widening: new server, re-enable, tool added, url/transport/command/args/env changed, pin removed or changed, integrity removed or changed, per_user_provider set or changed, mode lowered, unregistered_server set to allow, a require_* flag turned off. Narrowing: tool removed, pin or integrity added, disable, mode raised, a require_* flag turned on. Anything unrecognised is widening. A rollback that re-adds a tool removed during an incident is therefore held for a second approver. With approvals disabled the Gate clears every write and it applies directly.
- Distribution: when enabled the CP adds signed-bundle section `mcpRegistry` = {schema: "warden-mcp-registry/v1", revision, mode, unregisteredServer, requireStdioIntegrity, requirePinVerified, servers:[{id, version, transport, url, command, args, env, perUserProvider, approvedTools, toolPins, integrity}]}, holding the current versions of active servers only, sorted by id, with no author or approver fields. Every revision bump appends a `policy_publish_log` row with reason `mcp_registry` inside the registry write transaction (W-P2-SBND-02), so seq moves forward and long-poll waiters wake. The ETag scheme and the legacy wire are untouched. Mode lives inside the section, so a worker can never see mode=enforce without the server list. Only pinned workers receive it; the fleet view flags workers that lack cap `mcpregistry/v1` or report an older `mcpRegistryRevision`.
- Worker apply: after `bundle.Verify`, the section is compiled once into an immutable `mcpregistry.Compiled` (host to serverID map, id map, per-server approved-tool set and pin map). A section that fails to compile rejects the whole bundle with the existing reason `malformed` and keeps last-known-good, so a worker never applies new policy while silently dropping the registry. No section means no registry checks (today's behaviour); a section with mode off means no checks; a section with zero servers and mode enforce means every MCP server is unregistered. Heartbeat gains `mcpRegistryRevision`, `mcpRegistryActive` (false when `mcp.enabled` is false, so the gateway is nil) and cap `mcpregistry/v1`. Metrics `warden_mcp_registry_revision` and `warden_mcp_registry_findings_total{kind}`.
- Gateway enforcement (hot path is O(1) map reads; pin hashing only on tools/list, bounded by MaxResponseScanBytes): the gateway holds the Compiled in an `atomic.Pointer` set by `WithRegistry` and updated by `SetRegistry`, so a registry-only change does not reset sessions. OnRequest resolves serverID once per session, from `WithServerID` when set (wedge, MCP gateway hub) or else from the lowercased host in the session key, and stores it on the session; an unknown host gives `mcp_unregistered_server`. tools/list is never denied for registry reasons: tools outside approvedTools give `mcp_unregistered_tool`, and a pin mismatch gives `mcp_schema_drift` with Detail `registry_pin` and marks (serverID, tool) drifted gateway-wide, from the first list after start; a later matching list clears it. tools/call to an unregistered server, an unapproved tool or a drifted tool is denied; with requirePinVerified, a call to a tool whose pin has not been checked since start is also denied. Registry findings block only when both the gateway mode and the registry mode are enforce; unregisteredServer=allow downgrades only that finding. Existing poisoning, session-baseline drift and ToolPolicy behaviour stay as they are.
- Wedge (`warden mcp --server <id>`): the registry comes from `--registry-bundle <file>`, else a one-shot pinned pull through the --config controlPlane block (5s timeout), else the verified W-P2-SBND-06 bundle cache file under `controlPlane.stateDir` within bundleCacheMaxAge, each checked with `bundle.Verify` against `controlPlane.bundleKeys`. If a source is configured but nothing verifies, or `--require-registry` is set and no registry loads, the wedge refuses to launch. When the id is in the registry, its integrity for runtime.GOOS/GOARCH (or `any`) is mandatory, the resolved command must equal the registry `command`, and the args must equal the registry args. Local `mcp.servers` and `--verify-*` flags can only add checks; a flag that conflicts with a registry value is an error. On Linux the wedge hashes and execs the same open file descriptor (/proc/self/fd/N) to close the check-then-exec race. The gateway runs with `WithServerID(id)` and session key `stdio:<id>`. With no registry source configured, today's behaviour is unchanged. Docs state that the wedge is a cooperative control and the egress proxy remains the boundary, and that integrity on an interpreter (`node`, `npx`, `uvx`) proves nothing about the script it runs.
- Console (internal/dashboard): a Registry tab with server list, detail with version history (author from created_by_sub, approvers from change_approvals), structural diff, disable, enable and rollback, each of which may return a draft link. Import-from-observed reads new `mcpStore.Observed(host)`, which aggregates every worker's snapshot by (server host, tool) with worker count, first and last seen, and a conflict flag when workers report different pins; conflicted tools and tools without a `Pin` cannot be imported. For stdio, `warden mcp inspect -- <cmd>` runs initialize and tools/list once and prints tool names and pins as JSON to paste. All strings are rendered with textContent. The console warns when a registered http/sse/ws host is not in the egress allowlist, because registration never opens egress.
- Audit and observability: every write goes through the admin audit middleware with target_ref `mcp_server:<id>@v<N>` or `mcp_registry@r<rev>`, an `mcp_registry` StateHasher over (revision, section digest), and details {revision, from_version, to_version, widening, reasons}. slog `mcp_registry_change` carries ids, versions, revision and actor_sub only, never env values, args or integrity material. Worker registry findings flow into analytics with server id and tool name only. CP counters (registry writes, held drafts) are kept in memory as hooks for W-P5-RETN-06.
- Degraded modes: CP down means workers keep the last verified registry, and a stale bundle follows `bundleExpiry` keep|deny. IdP down means reads and enforcement continue; widening writes wait unless break-glass emergency apply is enabled (W-P2-APPR-07). Worker restart restores the registry from the opt-in bundle cache (W-P2-SBND-06), otherwise boot is fail-closed as today; drift marks are rebuilt from the next tools/list. Clock skew is handled by bundle issuedAt/expiresAt; registry ordering uses revision and version integers only. After a CP restore, `--bundle-seq-floor` applies as for any bundle.

## Done when

On a CP with console.auth=oidc, admin audit, --policy-store=versioned, --bundles=require, approvals enabled and console.mcpRegistry.enabled=true, an admin registers an HTTP server and a stdio server with approved tools and canonical pins (imported from observed inventory and from `warden mcp inspect`), and a second approver approves them. A pinned worker receives the `mcpRegistry` section under a new publish_log seq and reports the registry revision in its heartbeat. With the gateway and the registry both in enforce, the worker denies a tools/call to an unapproved tool, to a tool whose description or schema differs from its pin (detected on the first tools/list after a fresh start), and to an unregistered MCP host, while other tools on the same server keep working. The wedge refuses a stdio binary whose hash differs from the registry, refuses when the registry cannot be verified, and rejects CLI flags that conflict with registry integrity. A narrowing rollback applies at once and workers converge within one long-poll; a rollback that re-adds a tool is held as a draft. Every write has a chained admin audit row. With the registry disabled, `--bundles=off`, or an unpinned worker, /policy bytes and MCP behaviour are unchanged from the previous release.

### 1/10 · W-P4-MREG-01

**Add MCP registry data model, validation and store**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#177](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/177)

Create new package internal/mcpregistry with the server and version types, validation and a Store interface, plus a SQLite store in new internal/mcpregistry/sqlitestore. Endpoint and launch fields live on the immutable version row, so diff, approvals and rollback cover them. Validation rejects anything that could carry a real credential or redirect a child process, and integrity hex is checked by a new shared config helper, because none exists today. Nothing is wired to HTTP or the bundle, so merging changes no behaviour.

**Requirements**

- Types `Server{ID, Name, OwnerTeam, State active|disabled, CurrentVersion int, CreatedAt}`, `Version{ServerID, Version int, Transport http|sse|ws|stdio, URL, Command, Args []string, Env map[string]string (ENV name to placeholder), PerUserProvider, ApprovedTools []string, ToolPins map[string]string, Integrity map[string]Integrity (key `<GOOS>/<GOARCH>` or `any`), Label, DraftID, CreatedBySub, CreatedAt, DocSHA256}` and `Settings{Revision, Mode off|monitor|enforce, UnregisteredServer deny|allow, RequireStdioIntegrity, RequirePinVerified}` (defaults monitor, deny, true, false). internal/mcpregistry imports no DB code.
- `Store`: ListServers, GetServer, CreateServer, AddVersion (assigns max+1, never changes current), GetVersion, ListVersions, SetCurrent(id, version, expectedCurrent), SetState(id, state, expectedCurrent), GetSettings, PutSettings(s, expectedRevision) and Current() returning active current versions plus Settings. SetCurrent, SetState and PutSettings bump `revision` in the same transaction and return ErrConflict when the expected value moved.
- `Validate(v Version, ctx ValidateContext{Placeholders, ProviderIDs})`: https url for http/sse/ws (http only for loopback), no userinfo, no query value or arg or label matching the internal/scan credential detectors; stdio needs an absolute command and no url; env keys match ^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$ and are not reserved (PATH, LD_*, DYLD_*, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR); env values are in ctx.Placeholders; PerUserProvider, when set, is in ctx.ProviderIDs.
- Tools are 1..128 chars and unique; every pin key is an approved tool; pins match ^c1:[0-9a-f]{64}$. With RequireStdioIntegrity a stdio version needs at least one integrity entry. Integrity is checked by new exported `config.ValidateMCPIntegrity(prefix, sha256, pub, sig string) error` (64 hex, 64 hex not all-zero, 128 hex, signature needs key), and `validateMCPServers` in internal/config/mcp.go calls it too.
- Caps: 500 servers, 1000 approved tools per version, 64 args of at most 1024 bytes, 32 env entries, 256 KiB per serialized version. Errors name the field and index, never the value.
- sqlitestore registers cpstate migration `mcp_registry/0001` (tables mcp_servers, mcp_server_versions, mcp_registry_meta) through the W-P1-SSO-01 migrate API and offers `WithTxHook(func(ctx, *sql.Tx, reason string) error)`, run inside every revision-bumping transaction, for W-P4-MREG-05. A partial unique index rejects two active http/sse/ws servers whose current version has the same host.
- Conformance suite `mcpregistrytest.Run(t, newStore)` covers versioning, CAS conflicts, revision bumps, duplicate hosts and concurrent AddVersion, so p5-postgres-ha can reuse it.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/mcpregistry/types.go with Server, Version, Integrity, Settings and errors ErrNotFound, ErrConflict, ErrInvalid.
2. New internal/mcpregistry/validate.go with Validate and ValidateContext, reusing the internal/scan credential detectors for url, args and labels.
3. internal/config/mcp.go: extract new exported ValidateMCPIntegrity and call it from validateMCPServers; extend internal/config/mcp_test.go.
4. New internal/mcpregistry/store.go with the Store interface.
5. New internal/mcpregistry/sqlitestore/store.go with the migration, the Store implementation and WithTxHook.
6. New internal/mcpregistry/mcpregistrytest/run.go conformance suite, run from sqlitestore/store_test.go.
7. New internal/mcpregistry/validate_test.go table tests and FuzzValidateVersion.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given server `linear` at current version 1, AddVersion returns 2 and GetServer still reports CurrentVersion 1; SetCurrent(linear, 2, expectedCurrent 1) succeeds and bumps revision, and a second SetCurrent with expectedCurrent 1 returns ErrConflict.
- [ ] A stdio version without a command, a stdio version without integrity while RequireStdioIntegrity is true, an http version with a command, a 63-hex sha256 and an all-zero ed25519 public key are each rejected with an error naming the field.
- [ ] An env value that is not a known placeholder, an env key `LD_PRELOAD`, a url `https://x.example/mcp?api_key=sk-live-...` and an arg containing an AWS secret key are rejected, and the error text does not contain the value.
- [ ] Two active http servers on https://mcp.example.com/a and https://mcp.example.com/b are rejected as a duplicate host.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/mcpregistry/... ./internal/config -run 'TestValidate|TestStore|TestConformance|TestValidateMCPIntegrity'` passes, and `go test ./internal/mcpregistry -run '^$' -fuzz FuzzValidateVersion -fuzztime 30s` finds no panic.

### 2/10 · W-P4-MREG-02

**Add registry REST API with versioning, diff and rollback**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#178](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/178)

Mount the registry routes under `/dashboard/api/mcp/*` with the W-P2-APIK-02 Scope column behind the default-off `console.mcpRegistry.enabled` gate, with authz rows that set role, Scope `mcp:read` or `mcp:write`, and audit. Fields that decide what runs on worker hosts or where credentials go need admin. Writes use If-Match so two editors cannot race. This ticket applies writes directly; W-P4-MREG-03 routes them through approvals.

**Requirements**

- Config: `MCPRegistry ConsoleMCPRegistry{Enabled bool; MaxServers int; MaxToolsPerVersion int}` (`json:"-"`) on the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig, default disabled. When enabled, cmd/proxy/controlplane.go fails startup naming the missing item unless --state-dir, console.auth=oidc, console.adminAudit.enabled=true and --policy-store=versioned are set; the `--bundles` check is added in W-P4-MREG-05. When disabled, no migration runs and every /dashboard/api/mcp/* route returns 404.
- Routes: GET /dashboard/api/mcp/servers, GET /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/{id}, GET .../{id}/versions, GET .../{id}/versions/{v}, GET .../{id}/versions/{v}/diff?against={w} (default v-1), GET /dashboard/api/mcp/registry/settings (viewer, Scope mcp:read); POST /dashboard/api/mcp/servers, POST .../{id}/versions, POST .../{id}/rollback {version}, POST .../{id}/disable, POST .../{id}/enable, PUT /dashboard/api/mcp/registry/settings (editor minimum, Scope mcp:write). Rollback adds a new version copied from the target, so history stays append-only.
- Each route has a W-P1-SSO-05 authz row with Action `mcp_registry.<verb>`, Target `mcp_registry`, Audited:true on writes and an explicit Scope; the W-P2-APIK-02 TestAuthzRouteCoverage fails on an unclassified route. `mcp:read` and `mcp:write` are registered with the W-P2-APIK-01 scope registry at viewer and editor.
- Admin is required to create or enable a server, to change transport, url, command, args, env, integrity or per_user_provider, and to lower a registry setting; otherwise 403 `{"error":"role_required","need":"admin","fields":[...]}`.
- Server writes require If-Match `"v<current_version>"` and settings writes `"r<revision>"`: 409 `{"error":"registry_conflict","current":n}` when stale, 428 when missing. Bodies are capped at 1 MiB, unknown fields give 400, validation errors 422 `{"error":"invalid","field":"..."}`. Validate gets placeholders from live settings secrets and provider ids from `consent.providers`.
- Diff returns {addedTools, removedTools, addedPins, changedPins, removedPins, endpointChanged, commandChanged, argsChanged, envChanged, integrityChanged, perUserProviderChanged}, with pins as 16-hex prefixes and env as names only.
- Admin audit: `RegisterStateHasher("mcp_registry", ...)` hashes revision and the projected section digest; handlers call adminaudit.Annotate with target_ref `mcp_server:<id>@v<n>` or `mcp_registry@r<rev>` and details {revision, from_version, to_version}. Each write logs `msg=mcp_registry_change` with server id, versions, revision and actor_sub only.
- Example: POST /dashboard/api/mcp/servers/linear/rollback with If-Match "v3" and {"version":2} returns 200 {"server":"linear","version":4,"revision":9}; stale If-Match returns 409; a viewer gets 403 role_required; an mcp:read key gets 403 `{"error":"insufficient_scope","need":"mcp:write"}`.

**Implementation plan**

### 3/10 · W-P4-MREG-03

**Route widening registry changes and rollbacks through approvals**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#179](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/179)

Register `mcp_registry` as an approvals target with its own Classifier and Applier, following W-P2-APPR-08, so a widening registry write becomes a draft that needs a second approver. Every write is classified against the live current version, rollbacks included, so a rollback cannot quietly re-enable a tool removed during an incident. Pending changes live in change_drafts, not in mcp_server_versions. With approvals disabled, W-P4-MREG-02 behaviour is unchanged.

**Requirements**

- Target `mcp_registry` (target_ref = server id, or `settings` for registry settings) is registered with the APPR-08 target registry. Draft doc_json = {server_id, base_version, base_revision, proposed Version or Settings}; env holds placeholder names only, so no credential is stored.
- `mcpregistry.Classify(current, candidate)` is pure and deterministic with reasons sorted by code. Widening codes: mcp.server.created, mcp.server.enabled, mcp.tool.added, mcp.endpoint.changed (transport, url), mcp.command.changed (command, args), mcp.env.changed, mcp.pin.removed, mcp.pin.changed, mcp.integrity.removed, mcp.integrity.changed, mcp.provider.changed, mcp.settings.lowered. Narrowing: tool removed, pin or integrity added, label changed, disable, a setting raised. Any unrecognised difference is widening.
- RequiredRole is admin when the change creates or enables a server, touches transport, url, command, args, env, integrity or per_user_provider, or lowers a setting; editor otherwise.
- POST versions, rollback, enable and PUT settings go through approvals.Gate. With approvals enabled, a widening write returns 202 {draft_id, revision, state, widening, reasons} with a Location header to the draft; a narrowing write applies at once with decision `self` when allowSelfApproveNarrowing is true. Disable is always narrowing.
- The Applier re-reads current_version (or revision for settings); if it differs from the draft's base it returns ErrRebaseRequired and the draft moves to needs_rebase. Otherwise it runs AddVersion plus SetCurrent (or PutSettings) in one transaction with draft_id recorded, then calls the onChange hook.
- The two-person rule, the acknowledgeNoReplay evidence rule, audit details and Findings from W-P2-APPR-04 apply unchanged; fleet replay does not cover this target.
- Classify takes under 5 ms for 1000 tools per side and runs only on draft create, update, rebase and apply.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/mcpregistry/classify.go: Classify returning approvals.Classification, plus classify_test.go.
2. New internal/controlplane/approvals_mcpregistry.go: register the target, Classifier and Applier.
3. internal/controlplane/mcpregistry_api.go: route versions, rollback, enable and settings writes through approvals.Gate and return 202 when held.
4. Record draft_id on applied versions so history can list approvers from change_approvals.
5. New internal/controlplane/approvals_mcpregistry_test.go covering held, self-applied, role and rebase cases.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given approvals enabled and linear at v2, a POST version adding tool `delete_issue` returns 202 and current stays 2; a second editor's approval sets current to 3 and the version's draft_id links to that approval.
- [ ] A POST version that only removes a tool returns 201 and applies at once with change_approvals decision `self`.
- [ ] The author approving their own draft gets 403 `self_approval_forbidden`; a draft changing a stdio command approved by an editor gets 403 `role_required`, and an admin approval applies it.
- [ ] Given v3 removed tool X after an incident, a rollback to v2 (which has X) returns 202 with reason mcp.tool.added.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/mcpregistry ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestClassifyMCPRegistry|TestApprovalsMCPRegistry'` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MREG-02`](mcp-registry.md#210--w-p4-mreg-02) Add registry REST API with versioning, diff and rollback; [`W-P2-APPR-06`](policy-approvals.md#69--w-p2-appr-06) Gate every versioned write path through one clearance check; [`W-P2-APPR-08`](policy-approvals.md#89--w-p2-appr-08) Hold block-list removals and widening agent edits for approval

### 5/10 · W-P4-MREG-05

**Publish the registry as a signed-bundle section**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#181](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/181)

On the CP, add the `mcpRegistry` named section to the W-P2-SBND-02 bundle and append a `policy_publish_log` row with reason `mcp_registry` on every registry revision, instead of hashing the registry into the ETag. Mode travels inside the section, so a worker never sees enforce without the server list. The legacy wire is untouched, so unpinned workers and `--bundles=off` are unchanged. CP only; the worker side is W-P4-MREG-07.

**Requirements**

- Startup fails with an error naming `--bundles` when console.mcpRegistry.enabled is true and --bundles is off.
- buildBundle adds `sections.mcpRegistry` = {schema "warden-mcp-registry/v1", revision, mode, unregisteredServer, requireStdioIntegrity, requirePinVerified, servers[]} from Store.Current(): active current versions only, sorted by id, with no author, approver or label fields. With the registry disabled there is no section.
- The sqlitestore WithTxHook appends a publish_log row (current policy head version, reason `mcp_registry`, actor_sub) inside every revision-bumping transaction; after commit the onChange hook calls policyServer.Refresh so seq increases and long-poll waiters wake within 1s.
- A write whose projected section exceeds 1 MiB or would push the envelope over 4 MiB is refused with 422 `registry_too_large` before commit; a Refresh that still fails keeps the previous envelope, logs `mcp_registry_publish_failed` with revision only, and marks /healthz degraded.
- Heartbeat handling stores optional `mcpRegistryRevision` and `mcpRegistryActive` in WorkerRegistry; the fleet API adds `registryBehind` (revision below head, or cap `mcpregistry/v1` missing while enabled) and `registryInactive` (registry mode enforce but mcpRegistryActive false). Old workers keep working.
- The legacy policyWire never carries the registry, and /policy bytes are byte-identical with the registry disabled.

**Implementation plan**

1. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the `--bundles` prerequisite check and wire sqlitestore.WithTxHook to the publish_log append.
2. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go buildBundle: add the section from Store.Current().
3. internal/controlplane/policystore.go: accept reason `mcp_registry` on the publish_log append.
4. internal/controlplane/mcpregistry_api.go: set onChange to policyServer.Refresh and add the size check.
5. internal/controlplane heartbeat handler and WorkerRegistry: store the new fields and expose registryBehind and registryInactive.
6. New internal/controlplane/policyserver_mcpregistry_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given the registry enabled and --bundles=offer, SetCurrent of linear v3 appends one publish_log row with reason `mcp_registry`, and the next envelope has a higher seq whose `mcpRegistry` section lists linear at version 3.
- [ ] Flipping one byte inside the section of a served envelope makes bundle.Verify fail with bad_signature.
- [ ] `--bundles=off` with console.mcpRegistry.enabled=true fails CP startup with an error naming `--bundles`; with the registry disabled, /policy legacy bytes match the pre-change golden.
- [ ] A worker heartbeat with mcpRegistryRevision below head shows registryBehind=true in GET fleet.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestBundleMCPRegistrySection|TestMCPRegistryPublishLog|TestMCPRegistryTooLarge|TestFleetRegistryBehind'` passes.

### 6/10 · W-P4-MREG-06

**Enforce registry servers, tools and pins in the MCP gateway**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#182](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/182)

Add registry checks to the existing `Gateway.OnRequest` and `OnResponse` (keeping the W-P1-GPOL-04 `OnRequest(..., gateway.RequestMeta)` signature; no second OnRequest variant). The gateway resolves a server id once per session, observes tools/list without ever denying it for registry reasons, and denies tools/call per tool in enforce. A separate registry mode means switching the feature on cannot cause a fleet-wide deny, and a registry-only update does not reset sessions. Worker only.

**Requirements**

- New options `gateway.WithRegistry(*mcpregistry.Compiled)` and `gateway.WithServerID(id string)`, plus `(*Gateway).SetRegistry(*mcpregistry.Compiled)` storing into an atomic.Pointer. A nil registry, or mode off, runs no registry check, so behaviour is unchanged.
- OnRequest resolves serverID before the tools/call early return, once per session: the WithServerID value if set, else the lowercased host from the session key (serverFromSessionKey) looked up in the Compiled host map; it stores the id on the session. No match gives high `mcp_unregistered_server`.
- OnResponse tools/list: tools outside approvedTools give `mcp_unregistered_tool`; a tool whose `mcp.ToolPin` differs from its registry pin gives `mcp_schema_drift` with Detail `registry_pin` and marks (serverID, tool) drifted gateway-wide, starting from the first list; a matching list clears the mark. These findings never make the list itself blocking.
- tools/call is denied, before ToolPolicy evaluation, for an unregistered server, a tool not in approvedTools, a drifted tool, or (with requirePinVerified) a tool whose pin has not been checked since start. Deny requires both gateway Mode enforce and registry mode enforce; unregisteredServer=allow downgrades only that finding. The checks only add denies.
- internal/worker/applier.go SettingsApplier.Apply passes WithRegistry with the current Compiled when it rebuilds the gateway, and calls SetRegistry when only the registry changed. The local-only boot path is unchanged.
- New finding kinds are added to the bounded kind list in gateway.go; counter `warden.mcp.registry.findings.total{kind}` (exported `warden_mcp_registry_findings_total`) uses only the three registry kinds, with no tool label. Findings carry server id and tool name only.
- Hot path: map reads only; BenchmarkOnRequestRegistry adds under 1µs and 0 allocs per op over BenchmarkOnRequest.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/mcp/gateway/registry.go: options, SetRegistry, resolveServer and the drift mark map keyed by (serverID, tool).
2. internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go OnRequest (line 646): resolve and store serverID on the session, then add the tools/call checks.
3. internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go OnResponse tools/list branch: compute ToolPin per tool, emit findings and update drift marks; extend the finding kind comment.
4. internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go applyMode: combine gateway mode with registry mode for registry findings.
5. internal/observability: add the findings counter, nil-safe on *Metrics.
6. internal/worker/applier.go: pass WithRegistry and call SetRegistry on registry-only changes.
7. New internal/mcp/gateway/registry_test.go and an internal/worker/applier_test.go case.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given gateway and registry both enforce and linear approving [search], a tools/call for `delete_issue` to mcp.linear.app returns Deny with reason mcp_unregistered_tool; with registry mode monitor it returns Pass with the same finding.
- [ ] Given a pin for `search` and a first tools/list after start advertising `search` with a changed description, the list passes with mcp_schema_drift Detail `registry_pin`, a following tools/call to `search` in a new session is denied, and a call to another approved tool on the same server passes.
- [ ] Given a registry without mcp.other.com, a tools/call to it yields mcp_unregistered_server; with a nil registry the same call yields no registry finding.
- [ ] After SetRegistry with a new revision, existing session state is kept, and after a settings change the applier rebuilds the gateway with the registry.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/mcp/gateway ./internal/worker -run 'TestRegistry|TestApplierPassesRegistry' -bench BenchmarkOnRequestRegistry -benchmem` passes.

### 7/10 · W-P4-MREG-07

**Verify and compile the registry section on the worker**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Split from W-P4-MREG-05 so the worker side is its own PR. After `bundle.Verify`, the worker parses the `mcpRegistry` section, compiles it once into an immutable `mcpregistry.Compiled`, stores it in the same snapshot as policy, and reports its revision. An invalid section rejects the whole bundle and keeps last-known-good, so a worker never applies new policy while dropping the registry. Nothing is enforced until W-P4-MREG-06.

**Requirements**

- New `mcpregistry.ParseSection(raw json.RawMessage) (*Compiled, error)` reuses Validate (without the placeholder and provider checks, which are CP-only), and builds the host map, id map, approved-tool sets and pin maps. Unknown schema values are rejected.
- internal/config/remote.go: after bundle.Verify, a present section is parsed and stored in the immutable snapshot; a section that fails to parse rejects the bundle with reason `malformed` and keeps last-known-good. Unpinned (legacy) pulls never expose a registry.
- New accessor `MCPRegistry() *mcpregistry.Compiled` on RemoteProvider and the ControlPlaneClient interface in internal/worker/loops.go; nil when absent.
- Heartbeat adds `mcpRegistryRevision`, `mcpRegistryActive` (false when mcp.enabled is false) and cap `mcpregistry/v1`, keeping the body under 4096 bytes.
- Gauge `warden.mcp.registry.revision` (exported `warden_mcp_registry_revision`) and one INFO `mcp registry applied` with seq, revision and server count; never URLs, args, env or integrity material.
- The W-P2-SBND-06 bundle cache restores the section with the bundle, so a restarted worker keeps the registry.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/mcpregistry/wire.go and compiled.go with ParseSection and Compiled, plus wire_test.go.
2. internal/config/remote.go applyResponse: parse the section after verify and store it in the snapshot.
3. internal/worker/loops.go: add MCPRegistry to ControlPlaneClient; update the fake in loops_test.go.
4. Worker heartbeat builder: add the new fields and cap.
5. internal/observability: add the revision gauge.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A verified bundle with a valid section makes MCPRegistry() return a Compiled with the right revision, and the heartbeat carries that revision and cap `mcpregistry/v1`.
- [ ] A validly signed section containing a stdio server without a command is rejected as malformed, warden_bundle_rejected_total{reason="malformed"} increments, and the previous policy and registry stay applied.
- [ ] A bundle with no section, or a legacy-wire pull, yields MCPRegistry() == nil.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/mcpregistry ./internal/config ./internal/worker -run 'TestParseSection|TestRemoteProviderMCPRegistry|TestHeartbeatMCPRegistry'` passes.

### 8/10 · W-P4-MREG-08

**Make the warden mcp wedge enforce registry integrity**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue —

Split from W-P4-MREG-06. The `warden mcp` wedge only reads local YAML today (cmd/proxy/mcp.go loadMCPConfig) and lets `--verify-*` flags override config, so it needs its own verified registry source and a rule that local flags can only add checks. A named registry entry fixes the command, args, per-platform integrity, approved tools and pins. With no registry source configured, the wedge behaves as today.

**Requirements**

- Registry source order: `--registry-bundle <file>`; else a one-shot pinned pull through the --config controlPlane block (RemoteProvider.Pull, 5s timeout); else the W-P2-SBND-06 bundle cache file under `controlPlane.stateDir` (the one worker state dir) within bundleCacheMaxAge. Each is checked with bundle.Verify against controlPlane.bundleKeys and then mcpregistry.ParseSection.
- If a source is configured but nothing verifies, or `--require-registry` is set and no registry loads, the wedge exits non-zero before launch with an error naming the source. With no source configured and no --require-registry, behaviour is unchanged.
- For `--server <id>` present in the registry: the entry must be stdio; exec.LookPath of the server command must equal the registry command; args must equal the registry args; integrity for runtime.GOOS/GOARCH or `any` is mandatory and verified with stdio.VerifyBinary and VerifyEd25519. Local mcp.servers and --verify-* flags only add checks; a flag that conflicts with a registry value is refused.
- For an id not in a loaded registry: refuse when registry mode is enforce and unregisteredServer is deny; otherwise warn and fall back to local mcp.servers as today.
- On Linux the wedge opens the binary once, hashes from that descriptor and execs /proc/self/fd/N, closing the check-then-exec race; other platforms keep path exec and the docs say so.
- The gateway is built with WithRegistry and WithServerID(id), and the pump uses session key `stdio:<id>`, so approved tools and pins are enforced as in W-P4-MREG-06. Without --server the key stays `stdio`.

**Implementation plan**

1. cmd/proxy/mcp.go: add flags --registry-bundle and --require-registry and a new loadRegistry function for the source order.
2. cmd/proxy/mcp.go: replace resolveServerIntegrity with new resolveIntegrity(reg, servers, id, flags) that merges checks and refuses conflicts.
3. internal/mcp/stdio/integrity.go: add new VerifyFile(f *os.File, ...) used for the descriptor-based check.
4. cmd/proxy/mcp.go: exec via /proc/self/fd on Linux; pass WithRegistry, WithServerID and the new session key.
5. cmd/proxy/mcp_test.go: cases for mismatch, missing registry, conflicting flags, cache fallback and unapproved tool.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given registry entry `fs` with a linux/amd64 sha256 S and a binary whose hash differs, `warden mcp --server fs -- /opt/fs/bin` exits non-zero before launch.
- [ ] Passing `--verify-sha256 <other>` for a registry-managed id is refused with an error naming the flag.
- [ ] A tampered or expired `--registry-bundle` file makes the wedge exit non-zero; with no controlPlane block and no flags, an existing local-only test passes unchanged.
- [ ] With registry and gateway mode enforce, a tools/call to an unapproved tool through the wedge is denied.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy ./internal/mcp/stdio -run 'TestMCPRegistryIntegrity|TestMCPRegistryOverrideRefused|TestMCPRegistrySource|TestVerifyFile'` passes.

### 9/10 · W-P4-MREG-09

**Add canonical tool pins and server-keyed MCP inventory**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue —

Registry pins need a stable algorithm that also covers the tool description, because a changed description is how a tool is poisoned after approval, and raw-byte hashes break when a server re-serialises its schema. Add `mcp.ToolPin`, carry it through ToolInfo, InventoryItem and the CP snapshot, and key the gateway inventory by (server, tool) so two servers with the same tool name stop overwriting each other. Add `warden mcp inspect` so stdio servers can be pinned without traffic. Worker and CLI only; existing hashes and drift behaviour are unchanged.

**Requirements**

- New `mcp.ToolPin(name, description string, inputSchema json.RawMessage) (string, error)` = `c1:` + sha256 hex over canonical JSON (decode with UseNumber, sorted keys, no whitespace) of {name, description, inputSchema}. Invalid schema JSON returns an error.
- ToolInfo and InventoryItem gain `Pin` (omitempty), filled on every tools/list; `hashSchema` and InputSchemaHash stay unchanged.
- Gateway inventory is keyed by (Server, Name); Inventory() returns one item per pair. The persist_sqlite store adds an idempotent migration to a (server, name) key, keeping existing rows.
- analytics.MCPSnapshot carries the new field with no change to the ingest contract for old workers; the CP decodes snapshots without Pin as before.
- New `warden mcp inspect [--timeout 10s] -- <cmd> [args]` runs initialize and tools/list once against the child over stdio and prints {tools:[{name, pin}]} as JSON; it prints no descriptions or schemas and passes no extra environment.
- Canonicalisation is bounded by MaxResponseScanBytes and adds no work on tools/call.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/mcp/pin.go with ToolPin and pin_test.go (key order, whitespace and number-format invariance; description change changes the pin).
2. internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go: add Pin to ToolInfo and InventoryItem, fill it in the tools/list path, and key recordInventoryLocked by (server, name).
3. internal/mcp/gateway/persist_sqlite.go: migrate mcp_tools to a (server, name) key and store pin.
4. New cmd/proxy/mcp_inspect.go subcommand under newMCPCmd.
5. Tests in internal/mcp/gateway (two servers with the same tool name) and cmd/proxy (inspect against a fake stdio server).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Two inputSchema documents that differ only in key order and whitespace give the same ToolPin; changing the description gives a different pin.
- [ ] Two servers advertising `search` produce two inventory items with different Server values, and a persisted store from the previous release loads without loss.
- [ ] `warden mcp inspect -- ./testdata/fake-mcp` prints JSON with each tool's name and a `c1:` pin and exits 0.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/mcp ./internal/mcp/gateway ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestToolPin|TestInventoryByServer|TestPersistMigration|TestMCPInspect'` passes.

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-MREG-04`](mcp-registry.md#410--w-p4-mreg-04) Build console registry tab with import from observed inventory; [`W-P4-MREG-06`](mcp-registry.md#610--w-p4-mreg-06) Enforce registry servers, tools and pins in the MCP gateway

### 10/10 · W-P4-MREG-10

**Add MCP registry end-to-end test and operator docs**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue —

Prove the done_when across the CP, approvals, the signed bundle, a pinned worker and the wedge, and write the operator docs. The test covers registration with a second approver, per-tool denies, pin drift, an unregistered host, rollback in both directions and the audit chain. The docs cover the gate, rollout order, roles, pins and the limits of the wedge.

**Requirements**

- An integration test (build tag integration) runs an in-process CP with console.auth=oidc, admin audit, --policy-store=versioned, --bundles=offer, approvals enabled and console.mcpRegistry.enabled=true, two OIDC sessions (editor and admin), and a pinned long-polling worker in mcp enforce mode in front of a fake MCP server.
- It covers: register a server and approve its tools (two-person); the worker gets the section with a new seq and reports the revision; an approved call passes; an unapproved tool is denied; a description change against the pin is denied while another tool still passes; an unregistered host is denied; a narrowing removal applies at once; a rollback that re-adds a tool is held and then reaches the worker after approval.
- It runs the wedge against a fake stdio server with a matching and a mismatching hash.
- It asserts the admin audit chain verifies and that captured logs contain no env values, args or integrity material.
- New docs/mcp-registry.md and a docs/control-plane.md section cover the config keys and prerequisites, the rollout order (enable bundles and pin workers, enable the registry in monitor, register servers, then switch to enforce), roles, approvals, the pin algorithm, import limits, wedge registry sources and precedence, and that registration never opens egress.

**Implementation plan**

1. New test/integration/mcp_registry_test.go with the CP, worker and fake MCP server setup.
2. Reuse or extend the test/fakes MCP server to serve a changeable tool description and a stdio mode.
3. Add the wedge cases using the built binary and a --registry-bundle file written from the CP envelope.
4. Write docs/mcp-registry.md and update docs/control-plane.md and docs/architecture.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestMCPRegistryEndToEnd` passes, and after an approved rollback the worker enforces the previous approvedTools within 2s.
- [ ] The run shows zero `warden_bundle_rejected_total` increments.
- [ ] `warden control-plane admin-audit verify --state-dir <test dir>` reports ok with the registry rows in order.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check`.
